modmenu.descriptionTranslation.cobblemon: Real-time battles against wild Pokémon for Cobblemon, inspired by Pokémon Legends: Z-A. Beta: wild battles only for now.

cobblemon_combat_za.batalha.golpes_trava: 🔒 Moves can't be changed during a battle!

cobblemon_combat_za.soltar.sem_chao: 🚫 %s: there's no ground for it to land on
cobblemon_combat_za.guardas.descricao.pa: Passive: they just follow you, never attack
cobblemon_combat_za.guardas.descricao.ne: Neutral: they attack monsters that come close to you, and whatever you hit
cobblemon_combat_za.guardas.descricao.ag: Aggressive: they attack every monster nearby, even calm spiders, and whatever you hit

🛡 Everyone on guard: nobody selected, they all protect you

cobblemon_combat_za.golpe.descansou: %s fell asleep and restored all its HP! (+%s HP)
cobblemon_combat_za.status.hesitou_veloc: %s flinched, but its Speed won't go any higher: %s!
cobblemon_combat_za.habilidade.intimidou: %s intimidated %s: its Attack won't go any lower!
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.1.1: Here, battles aren't turn-based: they happen in real time, like in Pokémon Legends Z-A, against wild Pokémon, trainers and other players. You command your Pokémon with keys, and the other side fights back.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.1.2: These pages show the keys and how combat works. Below the text are the buttons for that page's keys: click one and press the new key. The "All keys" button shows them all together.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.2.1: The row at the bottom left is your team. %s and %s move the arrow; %s sends out the Pokémon under the arrow, or recalls it if it's already out. The item it holds shows in the bottom-right corner of its square. Each square also shows its level, gender and status.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.2.2: The one under the arrow, out of its ball, is your partner: it walks ahead of you, on your right, and only attacks when you tell it to. The others that are out are guards (page 7). Big ones walk further ahead, so they do not block your view.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.2.3: To make it walk on your left (and back): %s.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.2.3_sem_tec: To make it walk on your left, pick a key on the "Side" button below.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.3.1: Look at a wild Pokémon and press %s: your Pokémon lands halfway there and the battle starts. Hitting a wild Pokémon, or landing a move on it, also starts one.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.3.2: Wild Pokémon also notice you when they see you from the front (up close; even closer at night; crouching, they take twice as long): a "?" appears above them, and the eye at the top of the screen points to whoever is watching you. Only the fiercest ones come after you; the others only fight back, and the skittish ones run away; some move in herds. Wild Pokémon's moves deal 75% of the usual game damage to your Pokémon (the server can change this).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.3.3: In a battle, the panel at the top shows who fights whom, and the history below it tells every move. It ends when the wild Pokémon faints, is caught or gets far away (16 blocks). Running, you can escape: with none of your Pokémon out, the wild one is slower than you. If you run away, or if all your Pokémon faint, the ones that fought you leave you alone for 1 minute. Fighting a wild Pokémon registers it in your Pokédex as seen.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.4.1: %s %s %s %s use your Pokémon's 4 moves (the diamond on the right shows which ones).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.4.2: Each move charges before it goes off (the bar) and then cools down (the clock on the diamond). Contact moves run to the target (on a target in the air, flyers fly to it, and the others jump up to 3 blocks); ranged moves fire from where your Pokémon stands. Your moves pass through your allies, except area moves around the Pokémon (Earthquake, Surf), which hit allies for 75% of the damage. No move ever hits trainers (NPCs). Healing moves cool down for 10 seconds.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.4.3: In a battle, these keys always belong to your fighter, even with the arrow on another Pokémon.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.4.4: Riding: if the arrow is on your mount, the mount attacks. With a contact move, it runs to the target by itself and hits, and you get control back on the hit; ranged moves fire from where it stands.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.4.5: Hold a move key to see on the ground what it will hit, and release to use it. Changed your mind? %s cancels it, without the cooldown. A quick tap uses it right away, as always. The marking has an outline that shows on any ground; you can change its colors in Esc → HUD layout → Preview colors.
cobblemon_combat_za.previa.dica_marcador: Mouse: where it attacks from · Release: use · %s: cancel
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.5.1: Moves go where you are looking. Aimed at a wild Pokémon, flying moves curve after it (up close, a small target gets hit too).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.5.2: %s locks on to a wild Pokémon: the camera follows it and your moves go to it. While locked on, flick the mouse sideways to switch targets; %s again releases it. While locked on, the crosshair disappears.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.5.3: The wild Pokémon attacks you too: the colored bar above it warns you of the incoming move. Press %s twice, quickly, to roll and dodge (or %s).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.5.3_sem_tec: The wild Pokémon attacks you too: the colored bar above it warns you of the incoming move. Press %s twice, quickly, to roll and dodge.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.5.4: While locked on (%s), holding the key of a ranged or area move shows a blue circle on the ground: move the mouse to choose where your Pokémon will use the move from. When you release the key, it goes there and attacks. Red = it cannot see the target from there.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.6.1: In a battle, put the arrow on another Pokémon and press %s: your fighter goes back to its ball and the new one comes in. If the new one was already out, it joins right away, without the ball.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.6.2: Whoever switches in waits 2 seconds before attacking, like in the games. If your fighter fainted, the next one comes in ready.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.6.3: To just recall your fighter: put the arrow on it and press %s.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.7.1: Your other Pokémon out of their balls are guards: they protect you from monsters (zombies, skeletons, creepers...), never from the wild Pokémon in your battle. In Neutral and Aggressive, they also attack any creature you hit (even a villager or an iron golem, but never a trainer) until it falls, and anything that attacks you or them. The small row at the top of the screen shows who is on guard.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.7.2: Hold %s: the wheel picks their mode. Passive: they just follow you. Neutral: they attack monsters that come close to you. Aggressive: they attack every monster nearby.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.7.3: A quick tap on %s, outside a battle: everyone on guard (nobody is commanded, and they all protect you). A battle that starts turns it off by itself.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.8.1: The yellow arrows next to a wild Pokémon's brackets show the chance of the Poké Ball in your hand: 1 to 4 arrows; glowing means a sure catch. From behind (before it notices you) and with less health, it gets easier.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.8.2: %s + the mouse wheel: zooms the third-person camera in and out. In first person, scrolling down already switches to third person.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.8.3: That's it! The next page has all the keys together. To see this tutorial again, use the "Combat ZA Tutorial" button in the pause menu (Esc).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.9.1: Click a key and press the new one (Esc cancels; Delete leaves it unbound; the middle and side mouse buttons work too). Red: another action also uses that key; hover over it to see which.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.10.1: Defeating or catching a wild Pokémon gives XP, with Cobblemon's own formula, to every Pokémon of yours that was the fighter against it (switched mid-battle? both get it).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.10.2: Whoever holds an Exp. Share gets a part, even inside its ball or on guard. The Lucky Egg, EVs (with power items) and "defeat" evolutions also work, like in Cobblemon.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.10.3: The XP comes the moment each wild Pokémon falls, and at the end of the battle the notice shows how much each Pokémon got (and the new level, if it went up). Caught one without a battle, from behind? Your selected Pokémon that is out gets the full XP.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.11.1: With the Mega Bracelet equipped in your accessories and the Pokémon holding its Mega Stone, it can Mega Evolve. The Mega gauge (bottom right) tells you: it shows up when your Pokémon out of its ball can Mega Evolve, outside battles too.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.11.2: %s transforms your Pokémon. Outside battles, the selected one that is out, with no time limit (press it again to turn it back). In a battle, your fighter. The animation holds it still for a few seconds, taking no damage.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.11.2_sem_te: The Mega key (pick one on the "Mega" button below) transforms your Pokémon. Outside battles, the selected one that is out, with no time limit (press it again to turn it back). In a battle, your fighter. The animation holds it still for a few seconds, taking no damage.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.11.3: In a battle, the purple gauge (bottom right) starts full, and a Mega fighter uses it up, even one transformed with the Cobblemon wheel or before the battle: 1 minute, draining like a clock (recalling pauses it); then it turns back to normal. Afterwards the gauge refills: by itself in 2 minutes, and every hit your fighter lands speeds it up. While it is empty, your fighter cannot stay Mega. When the battle ends, a Mega Pokémon stays Mega. If it faints while Mega, it turns back to normal.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.12.1: In a battle, potions, revives and status cures work right away, but then you wait a few seconds (5, or what the mod's config says) to use another bag item. Outside battles, use them freely.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.12.2: X items (X Attack, X Speed, X Accuracy...) raise your fighter 2 stages until the battle ends.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.12.3: Special balls: the Quick Ball is ×5 before the battle and in its first 3.5 seconds; the Timer Ball gets better as the battle goes on (up to ×4 in 35 seconds); the Level and Love Balls compare with your fighter.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.12.4: Ether and Elixir: in battle, Ether makes the move you choose recharge 2× faster for 17.5 seconds, and Elixir does it for all 4 moves; Max Ether and Max Elixir reset the recharge right away. Against trainers, they restore PP as usual.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.13.1: The item a Pokémon holds works in battle, on yours and on wild ones. Type items (Charcoal, Mystic Water, Magnet...) make moves of that type 20% stronger; Muscle Band and Wise Glasses, physical or special moves, 10%; Expert Belt, super effective moves, 20%; Life Orb, every move, 30%, but each move that hits takes 1/10 of its HP.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.13.2: Choice Band, Specs and Scarf: Attack, Special Attack or Speed +50%, but the first move it uses in the battle becomes the only one (the others are crossed out) until it goes back to its ball. Assault Vest gives +50% Special Defense and turns off status moves; Eviolite gives +50% to both defenses of a Pokémon that can still evolve.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.13.3: Leftovers heal 1/16 of HP every 3.5 seconds (Black Sludge too, on Poison types; on others it hurts 1/8). Berries are eaten at the right moment: Oran, Sitrus and Berry Juice heal at half HP, the others cure the status. Focus Sash holds on with 1 HP against a hit that would knock it out at full HP (once per battle), and Rocky Helmet hurts whoever hits it with contact (1/6 of their HP).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.13.4: During a battle, giving or taking a Pokémon's held item counts as using a bag item: afterwards you wait a few seconds before using another.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.19.1: Resist berries (Occa, Passho, Wacan...) halve a super effective move of their type, once; the Chilan Berry, a Normal move.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.19.2: At 1/4 HP: Liechi, Ganlon, Salac, Petaya and Apicot raise a stat; Starf raises a random one; Lansat raises the critical hit rate; Micle, the next move's accuracy; Custap makes the next move go off without charging. Figy, Wiki, Mago, Aguav and Iapapa heal 1/3 of HP, and confuse those who dislike the flavor.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.19.3: When hit: Kee (physical) and Maranga (special) raise a defense; Jaboca and Rowap hurt the attacker; Enigma heals against a super effective move. Leppa makes one move recharge 2× faster, like an Ether.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.20.1: Gems make the first move of their type 30% stronger. Plates, Orbs, Soul Dew and the Masks boost the moves of their Pokémon; with a Plate, Memory or Drive, Judgment, Multi-Attack and Techno Blast change type.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.20.2: Scope Lens and Razor Claw raise the critical hit rate; Wide Lens and Zoom Lens, accuracy; Bright Powder makes foes miss more. Metronome: repeating the same move makes it up to 2× stronger. Loaded Dice: 2-to-5-hit moves hit 4 or 5 times. Punching Glove: stronger punches, without contact.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.20.3: Iron Ball and the Power items halve Speed. Quick Claw (sometimes) makes the move go off without charging; Lagging Tail makes charging slower; Power Herb makes Solar Beam go off at once outside the Sun.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.21.1: When hit: Air Balloon (immune to Ground) pops; Weakness Policy sharply raises Attack and Special Attack; Focus Band sometimes hangs on with 1 HP. Red Card sends the attacker out of the battle (the wild one flees); Eject Button and Eject Pack send your Pokémon back to its ball, and you send out the next.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.21.2: White Herb undoes stat drops; Mirror Herb copies the foe's stat boosts; Clear Amulet stops others from lowering your stats; Covert Cloak blocks the extra effects of moves.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.21.3: Each turn, Flame Orb burns and Toxic Orb badly poisons the holder; Sticky Barb hurts and sticks to whoever touches it. Seeds raise a defense on their terrain. Utility Umbrella: no Sun or Rain; Safety Goggles: no powder or sand; Heavy-Duty Boots: no hazards; Smoke Ball: fleeing is easier.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.14.1: In battle, the weather changes the moves. If it is raining where you are, under open sky, it is Rain: Water moves get 50% stronger and Fire moves weaker. If it is snowing, it is Snow: Ice types get more Defense. Under a roof, in a cave or in the desert, nothing. The weather shows as an icon above the team panel, with the seconds left.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.14.2: Rain Dance, Sunny Day, Sandstorm and Snowscape (or Hail) call the weather for 17.5 seconds (28 with a Damp, Heat, Smooth or Icy Rock), over the world's weather. In Sun, Fire gets strong and Water weak. In a Sandstorm, anyone who is not Rock, Ground or Steel loses a little HP every 3.5 seconds, and Rock types get Special Defense.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.14.3: The weather also changes other moves and abilities, as in the games: Thunder and Hurricane never miss in Rain, and Blizzard in Snow; Solar Beam charges 2 seconds longer outside the Sun; Weather Ball changes type; Moonlight and Synthesis heal more in the Sun. Swift Swim and Chlorophyll double the speed in Rain and Sun, and Drizzle and Drought call the weather when the Pokémon enters the battle.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.15.1: Electric, Grassy and Psychic Terrain make moves of their type 30% stronger for an attacker on the ground (flying or levitating Pokémon are left out). Grassy heals a little every 3.5 seconds and weakens Earthquake; Misty stops anyone on the ground from getting a status or confusion; on Electric nobody falls asleep; on Psychic, an enemy's priority move doesn't hit. They last 17.5 seconds (28 with a Terrain Extender).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.15.2: Screens protect one side of the battle: Reflect halves physical damage, Light Screen special damage, and Aurora Veil both (only in Snow); critical hits go through. Tailwind doubles speed, Safeguard stops status, Mist stops stats from being lowered and Lucky Chant stops critical hits. Screen icons have a blue border on your side and pink on the wild side.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.15.3: All of this also works outside battles, for your Pokémon out of their balls (against monsters, Reflect cuts their hits and Light Screen their magic). Whatever is active when a battle starts goes into it, and what is left comes back with you. The icons: ☂ Rain, ☀ Sun, ≈ Sand, ❄ Snow, ⚡ Electric, ✿ Grassy, ☁ Misty, ✦ Psychic, ◈ Reflect, ◇ Light Screen, ✧ Aurora Veil, ➶ Tailwind, ✚ Safeguard, ≋ Mist, ✪ Lucky Chant.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.16.1: A wild Pokémon that faints in battle stays down on the ground for 10 seconds: that is your only chance to catch it, with one Poké Ball. If the ball fails, or time runs out, it disappears. The XP and the items it drops come out the moment it falls.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.16.2: If a Poké Ball fails on an awake wild Pokémon, it comes out of the ball mad: it wakes up (if it was asleep), gets angry (the red vein above it) and the battle starts. While angry, it can't be caught: the ball comes back to you. To calm it down, your Pokémon must take some of its HP (15%; more for bold natures, less for calm ones), or wait 1 minute.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.17.1: Play with friends in a party of up to 4: /party convidar <name> (whoever invites becomes the leader), /party aceitar or the invite button in chat, /party sair, /party expulsar <name> (leader only) and /party to see who is in it.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.17.2: The party fights together: members within 32 blocks join your battle, and the XP of each wild Pokémon is split among you. Players outside your party can't join your battle, and your moves pass through them and their Pokémon. Area moves around the Pokémon (Earthquake) hit yours and the party's for 75% of the damage.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.17.3: Your party members glow green, even through walls, and show in a small panel on screen: you on top and, below, each one's name and health (the crown is the leader; the swords, whoever is in a battle). Whoever leaves the game stays in the party: they show greyed out, as offline, and are back in it when they join.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.17.4: Or press %s to open the party screen: invite someone from the list of online players (or by typing the name), answer an invite, leave and remove someone (the leader). When someone invites you, the invite also shows in the party panel.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.17.4_sem_te: Or pick a key on the "Party" button below to open the party screen: invite someone from the list of online players (or by typing the name), answer an invite, leave and remove someone (the leader). When someone invites you, the invite also shows in the party panel.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.17.5_opac: On this server, the party is the Open Parties and Claims one: the same that shares protected land. /party and the party screen work with it.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.18.1: With Xaero's map, the party shares waypoints. Open Xaero's waypoint menu, pick the "Party" set at the top (the game creates it for you) and create waypoints in it.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.18.2: They show on the minimap and map of everyone in your party, with your name ("Home (Victor)"). Delete or change one and it changes for everyone. Waypoints in your other sets stay yours only.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.18.3: The minimap only shows the selected set: to see all your sets together, turn on "Render All Waypoint Sets" in Xaero's options. The party's waypoints always show.

cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.22.1: Every part of the combat screen can be moved and resized: your Pokémon (with its HP), your team's row, the moves, the battle (the history), the guards, the party, the Mega, the weather effects and the eye of whoever notices you. On small screens, they already shrink on their own.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.22.2: In the pause menu (Esc), click "HUD layout". Drag a part to move it; pull one of the small white squares on the corners or edges to make it bigger or smaller. Pink lines help you line things up. With Alt, it resizes around the middle; the arrow keys move it 1 pixel. The bar with the buttons can be dragged by its background, and – collapses it into a small button.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.22.3: It is saved in your game: every time you join, it is just as you left it. "Reset block" and "Reset all" put things back in their usual place.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.23.1: Many abilities change a move's math, with the games' numbers. Power abilities multiply the move (Iron Fist on punches, Strong Jaw on bites, Sharpness on slicing moves, Tough Claws on contact; Sheer Force trades the extra effect for more power; Pixilate and similar ones turn Normal moves into their own type). Defensive ones cut the damage (Multiscale at full HP, Fluffy against contact, Ice Scales against special moves, Fur Coat).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.23.2: Some work for the whole battle while their owner is in it: the Ruin abilities weaken one stat of everyone else, and the Auras power up everyone's Dark or Fairy moves. What is "per turn" in the games happens every 3.5 seconds here: Stakeout hits twice as hard on someone who just switched in, and Analytic hits harder on someone who just attacked.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.23.3: Mold Breaker (and Teravolt and Turboblaze) ignores the target's abilities that would get in the way: Levitate doesn't save it from Earthquake, Sturdy doesn't hold the hit. Mega Kangaskhan's Parental Bond hits twice, and Gorilla Tactics locks the Pokémon into its first move, like a Choice Band.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.23.4: When a Pokémon enters the battle (the wild one arrives, your fighter is chosen or switched in), some abilities act right away: Anticipation warns if a foe has a super effective move against it, Forewarn reveals the foe's strongest move and Frisk shows each foe's item; Download, Intrepid Sword and Dauntless Shield raise a stat (the last two once per battle), Supersweet Syrup lowers the foes' Evasion and Screen Cleaner ends Reflect, Light Screen and Aurora Veil. The legendaries change the weather for good: Desolate Land brings an extremely harsh sun that evaporates Water moves, Primordial Sea a heavy rain that puts out Fire moves, and Delta Stream strong winds that protect the Flying type; these weathers last while their owner is on the field, and no weather move replaces them. Protosynthesis and Quark Drive boost the highest stat in Sun or on Electric Terrain (or with Booster Energy).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.23.5: Regenerator heals 1/3 of HP when going back to the ball after fighting; Emergency Exit and Wimp Out pull the Pokémon out of the fight when its HP drops below half (a wild one runs away). Arena Trap, Shadow Tag and Magnet Pull trap: while trapped, you need to get 24 blocks away to flee, and a trapped skittish wild Pokémon can't run. Several abilities stop moves: Soundproof (sound), Bulletproof (balls and bombs), Good as Gold (status), Wonder Guard (anything that isn't super effective), Wind Rider (wind, and it also raises Attack), Queenly Majesty, Dazzling and Armor Tail (fast moves), Magic Bounce (sends status moves back) and Damp (nobody explodes). Contrary reverses and Simple doubles stat changes; Mirror Armor bounces drops back; Competitive and Defiant go up 2 when a foe lowers a stat; Guard Dog gets stronger from Intimidate.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.23.6: Many abilities do something when the Pokémon takes a hit or knocks someone out. The one that was hit can get stronger (Stamina raises Defense, Justified raises Attack against Dark moves, Steam Engine shoots Speed up with Fire or Water), hinder the attacker (Gooey lowers Speed, Cursed Body disables the move for 14 seconds, Toxic Debris spreads Toxic Spikes under it, Perish Body makes both faint in 10.5 seconds) or steal its item (Pickpocket). Knocking out a Pokémon with a move makes the attacker stronger (Moxie, Beast Boost), and the one that falls can take the attacker with it (Aftermath, Innards Out). An item a wild Pokémon steals from yours comes back when the thief leaves the battle; what your Pokémon steals from a wild one is yours.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.23.7: Every 3.5 seconds, Speed Boost raises Speed, Moody shuffles stats, Bad Dreams hurts sleeping foes, Harvest regrows the eaten berry and Pickup grabs an item someone else just used up. For priority abilities, "moving first" becomes "the move goes off without charging": Prankster does it for status moves (which don't affect Dark types), Gale Wings for Flying moves at full HP, Triage for healing moves and Quick Draw on 30% of moves.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.23.8: Abilities that change a Pokémon mid-fight in the games work too, and you see it: Aegislash turns into Blade Forme when it attacks, Darmanitan enters Zen Mode at half HP, Wishiwashi forms a school, Minior drops its shell, Zygarde becomes Complete Forme, Mimikyu's disguise breaks on the first hit, and Castform and Cherrim change with the weather. The new form brings its own stats and type, and everything goes back to normal when the Pokémon returns to its ball or the battle ends.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.23.9: Some change the type (Protean and Libero take the move's type; Color Change, the type of the move that hit; Mimicry, the terrain's), others copy or swap the ability (Trace, Mummy, Wandering Spirit), and Neutralizing Gas silences everyone's abilities in the fight. Turn-based ones use the mod's turn (3.5 seconds): Truant leaves Slaking 3.5 seconds without moves after each move, and Slow Start halves Regigigas's Attack and Speed for the first 17.5 seconds.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.24.1: Taunt leaves the target without status moves for 10.5 seconds; Encore locks the target into the last move it used for the same time. On your Pokémon, blocked moves show crossed out on the diamond and the key does nothing. Attract only works between male and female: the infatuated Pokémon has a 50% chance of failing to attack (the move still cools down) until one of the two leaves the fight; the Cute Charm ability infatuates whoever touches it (30%). Oblivious and Aroma Veil protect, and a Mental Herb cures it at once.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.24.2: Trick Room lasts 17.5 seconds for everyone and turns speed inside out: with your Pokémon against a wild one, the two swap speeds for charging and cooling down moves; using it again undoes it. Skill Swap, Role Play, Entrainment, Simple Beam, Worry Seed and Gastro Acid swap (or erase) the ability until the Pokémon goes back to its ball.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.24.3: Brick Break, Psychic Fangs and Raging Bull break Reflect, Light Screen and Aurora Veil before the damage; Defog clears the target's screens, the traps and the terrain; Rapid Spin and Mortal Spin free the spinner and pick up nearby enemy traps; Tidy Up picks up all of them and raises Attack and Speed.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.25.1: When you talk to an RCT trainer (or they challenge you), a small screen opens: "Real time" or "Turn-based" (Esc: don't battle now). Turn-based is Cobblemon's usual battle. In real time, the trainer throws one Pokémon at a time near them, and you fight it like a wild one, with your keys; if you have no Pokémon out, the first one in your team comes out too. RCT double battles stay turn-based.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.25.2: The trainer's Pokémon only attacks your Pokémon (never you or NPCs), doesn't run away and can't be caught (the ball comes back). When it faints, you get the XP right away, it goes back to the trainer's ball and the next one comes out 2 seconds later. Strong trainers (gyms, Elite Four, champions) use the items in their bag, like Potions and Full Restore, with the same wait between items as you; a Pokémon holding a Mega Stone mega-evolves when it comes out, and one that would hold a Z-Crystal uses its backup item (Z-Moves don't exist in real time).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.25.3: Winning counts for RCT just like a turn-based battle: the series, the level cap and the reward. Losing (all your Pokémon fainted) or walking 24 blocks away from the trainer (with a warning at 16) counts as a defeat.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.26.1: A duel starts from Cobblemon's own challenge: look at the other player, press Cobblemon's send-out key (R) and, on the wheel, pick Battle → Singles and your lead Pokémon. A duel screen opens right away: choose how many Pokémon each side uses, from 1 to 6 (up to the smaller healthy team of the two); the other player is told in chat and accepts from their own wheel. Each side uses the lead chosen in the challenge and the next healthy ones, in team order; only they leave their balls until the end. Doubles, Triples and Multi stay turn-based, and the challenge's level rule (Level 50/100) doesn't apply in real time.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.26.2: The fight works like against a wild Pokémon: one fighter at a time, switching with R, cooldowns, items with their wait, weather, terrain, held items, abilities and Mega. Moves only hit the opponent's Pokémon: they pass through players, wild Pokémon, trainers and each side's party; lock-on and the nameplates only show the opponent's Pokémon. When a Pokémon faints, its owner sends the next one; after 15 seconds with nobody out, the next one goes in on its own. A Pokémon that faints in a duel doesn't lie on the ground and can't be caught.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.26.3: You lose when you run out of the chosen Pokémon; walking more than 24 blocks from the duel spot (with a warning first), leaving the game or dying counts as forfeiting. Each of the opponent's Pokémon that faints gives XP to whoever fought it (and to Exp. Share), with the same math as a wild one; the server can turn this off with Cobblemon's allowExperienceFromPvP option.
cobblemon_combat_za.layout.dica: Drag a block to move it. Pull the small squares on the corners or edges to resize it (with Alt, around the middle). Arrow keys: 1 pixel (with Shift, 10). Drag this bar by its background; – collapses it.
cobblemon_combat_za.cores.dentro: Fill (the first one: the move's type color)
cobblemon_combat_za.cores.contorno: Outline (the dark outer edge always stays)
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.1.1: Here, battles happen in real time, like in Pokémon Legends Z-A, against wild Pokémon, trainers and other players: you command your Pokémon with keys, and the other side fights back.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.1.2: These pages show the basics. Below each one are the buttons for its keys: click one and press the new key. The details (every item, the weather, catching...) are on the wiki: the button below.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.2.1: The row at the bottom left is your team. %s and %s move the arrow; %s sends out the Pokémon under the arrow, or recalls it. The one that is out is your partner: it walks beside you and only attacks when you tell it to.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.2.2: In a battle, put the arrow on another Pokémon and press %s to switch fighters: the one that comes in waits 2 seconds to attack.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.2.3: %s makes your partner walk on the other side.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.2.3_sem_t: To make your partner walk on the other side, pick a key on the "Side" button below.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.3.1: Look at a wild Pokémon and press %s (or hit it): the battle starts. The panel at the top shows who is fighting, and the history tells every move.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.3.2: Wild Pokémon notice you when they see you from the front: a "?" appears above them (crouching, they take longer). Only the fiercest come after you; the skittish ones run away.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.3.3: The battle ends when the wild Pokémon falls or is caught, or when you run far away (16 blocks). Defeating or catching gives XP, like in Cobblemon, and adds the wild Pokémon to your Pokédex.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.3.4: Some wild Pokémon trap yours (Arena Trap, Shadow Tag, Magnet Pull): to run away, get 24 blocks away instead of 16.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.3.5: Trainers: when you talk to one, choose "Real time" or "Turn-based". In real time they send one Pokémon at a time, which only attacks yours; winning counts for the series as usual, and walking 24 blocks away from them is forfeiting.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.4.1: %s %s %s %s use your fighter's 4 moves (the diamond on the right). Each move charges before it goes off (the bar) and then cools down (the clock).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.4.2: Hold the key to see on the ground what the move will hit, and release to use it; %s cancels. Contact moves run to the target; ranged moves fire from where the Pokémon is.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.4.3: Your moves pass through your allies and never hit trainers (NPCs).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.4.4: A move crossed out on the diamond is blocked right now (by a Choice item, Taunt or Encore): wait for it to wear off or switch Pokémon.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.4.5: Pokémon abilities work like in the games: they change damage, react to being hit, and some make a move go off without charging. What happens "per turn" there happens every 3.5 seconds here.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.5.1: Moves go where you look. %s locks on to a wild Pokémon: the camera follows it, and %s again releases it.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.5.2: The wild Pokémon attacks too: the colored bar above it warns you of the coming move. %s twice, quickly, makes you roll to dodge (or %s).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.5.2_sem_t: The wild Pokémon attacks too: the colored bar above it warns you of the coming move. %s twice, quickly, makes you roll to dodge.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.5.3: %s + the mouse wheel zooms the camera in and out.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.6.1: Your other Pokémon out of their balls are guards: they protect you from monsters and attack whatever you hit (never the wild Pokémon in your battle, nor trainers).
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.6.2: Hold %s to pick their mode: Passive, Neutral or Aggressive. A quick tap, outside a battle, puts everyone on guard.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.7.1: The arrows next to the wild Pokémon show the chance of the Poké Ball in your hand: 1 to 4; glowing means a sure catch. From behind, asleep or with low HP, it gets easier.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.7.2: If the ball fails, it comes out mad and the battle starts. A wild Pokémon that faints stays down for 10 seconds: your last chance to catch it.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.8.1: In a battle, potions, revives, X items and Ethers work right away, with a wait of a few seconds between one item and the next.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.8.2: Almost every held item works as in the games, on your Pokémon and on the wild one: type boosters, Choice items, berries, Gems, Focus Sash, Air Balloon and many more. The full list is on the wiki.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.9.1: Rain, Sun, Sandstorm and Snow change moves like in the games, and the world's rain and snow count too. Terrains (Electric, Grassy, Misty, Psychic) and screens (Reflect, Light Screen, Aurora Veil...) work as well.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.9.2: All of this shows as icons above your team, with the seconds left.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.9.3: In Trick Room (⇅), slow Pokémon become fast and fast ones become slow: the slow one charges and cools down faster.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.10.1: With the Mega Bracelet in your accessories and the Mega Stone on the Pokémon, %s transforms it.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.10.1_sem_: With the Mega Bracelet in your accessories and the Mega Stone on the Pokémon, the Mega key (pick one on the "Mega" button below) transforms it.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.10.2: In a battle, the purple gauge (bottom right) limits the Mega: it lasts 1 minute, and then the gauge fills up again.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.11.1: Play in a party of up to 4: %s opens the party screen (or use /party convidar <name>). Members nearby join your battle, and the XP is split.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.11.1_sem_: Play in a party of up to 4: /party convidar <name> (or pick a key on the "Party" button below to open the party screen). Members nearby join your battle, and the XP is split.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.11.2: The party shows in a small panel on screen and is saved: whoever leaves the game stays in it.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.11.3_xaer: With Xaero's map, the waypoints in the "Party" set show for everyone in the party.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.12.1: In the pause menu (Esc), "HUD layout" changes where and how big each part of the screen is: drag to move, pull the corners to resize. "Preview colors" for moves is there too.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.12.2: That's it! The next page has all the keys. To see this tutorial again: Esc → "Combat ZA Tutorial".
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.13.1: Look at another player, press %s and pick Battle → Singles: a screen asks how many Pokémon each side uses. Once they accept, the duel is in real time, like against a wild Pokémon.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.13.2: Moves only hit the other player's Pokémon. Fainted? Send the next one with %s (after 15 seconds it goes in on its own). You lose if you run out of Pokémon or go more than 24 blocks away.
cobblemon_combat_za.tutorial.c.13.3: Each of their Pokémon that faints gives your Pokémon XP, like a wild one.
